content: Dr. Endre Beogo, Director of the Disease Control Division, Dr. Sylvestre Tapsoba, Director of Nutrition, Dr. Moussa Dadjoari, Coordinator for Schistosomiasis, Dr. Emmanuel Seini, Specialist in Neglected Tropical Diseases, along with Mr. Hamado Ouedraogo and Mr. Clément T. Bagnoa from the Schistosomiasis Control Programme, were key contributors from Burkina Faso. Additionally, international and non-governmental organizations in Burkina Faso were represented by Dr. Ann Tarini, Country Director of Helen Keller International; Mr. Issouf Bamba, Project Coordinator for ONCHO-LF-Vitamin A; Dr. Seydou Toure, Country NTD Program Manager for RISEAL; Dr. Maurice Hours, Chief of the Health and Nutrition Programme at UNICEF; Dr. Biram N’Diaye, a nutrition specialist; and Dr. Alhousseyni Maiga, FP/CPC. The group acknowledged the significant contributions of Prof. Evariste Mutabatu, Acting Director of the WHO Multi-Disease Surveillance Centre (MDSC) in Burkina Faso, and Dr. Aimé Gilles Adjami, also from MDSC Burkina Faso. During a stakeholders' meeting in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, important input was provided by Dr. Zaida Yàdon, Regional Advisor on Communicable Diseases at CDC/PAHO/AMRO; Dr. Ottorino Cosivi from the Veterinary Public Health Unit at the Pan American Center for Foot and Mouth Disease (PANAFTOSA); Dr. Naftale Katz from the Ministry of Health in Rio de Janeiro; Dr. Robert Bergquist from Sweden; Dr. Otavio Pieri from the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (FIOCRUZ) in Rio de Janeiro; Dr. Philip LoVerde from the University of Texas Health Sciences Center in San Antonio, USA; Dr. Jeffrey Bethony from George Washington University, USA; Prof. P. Geldhof from the Department of Virology, Parasitology, and Immunology at Ghent University, Belgium; and Prof. Rodrigo Correa-Oliveira from the Rene Rachou Research Center at FIOCRUZ MG in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. The DRG4 group also expressed gratitude for the support of the African Programme for Onchocerciasis Control in Burkina Faso, which hosted the first DRG4 meeting. Key contributors included Dr. Uche Veronica Amazigo, Director; Dr. Laurent Yameogo, Coordinator of the Director’s Office; Dr. Mounkaila Noma, Chief of Epidemiology and Vector Elimination; Dr. Grace Fobi, Community Ownership and Partnership Officer; Dr. Stephen Leak, Technical Adviser; Mrs. Zainab Akiwumi, Communication and Advocacy Officer; Mr. Paul Ejime, Communication Officer; Dr. Afework Hailemariam Tekle, Epidemiologist; Mr. Saïdou N’Gadjaga, IT Help Desk Specialist; and Mr. Issaka Niadou Yacouba, Information System Officer. The group also benefited from the expertise of members of the Informal Consultation who helped define the scope of DRG4. These included Prof. Philip LoVerde from the University of Texas Health Sciences Center, Prof. Roger Prichard from McGill University, Prof. Rodrigo Correa-Oliveira from FIOCRUZ MG, Dr. Warwick Grant from La Trobe University in Australia, Prof. Xiao-Nong Zhou from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr. Daniel Boakye from the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research in Ghana, and Prof. Banchob Sripa from Khon Kaen University in Thailand. Dr. Mike Osei-Atweneboana, a WHO/TDR Career Development Fellow from the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research in Ghana, was instrumental in preparing this report. The group also extended their appreciation to the peer reviewers for their valuable comments and contributions to the technical accuracy of the report. Dr. Nina Mattock oversaw the technical editing of the document. The TDR provided both technical and financial support for the report, with additional financial backing from the European Commission under Agreement PP-AP/2008/160-163.
